Certified type:
- Category: Non-automatic weighing instrument (or "Weighing instrument"). The schema says category examples: "Load cell", "Indicator", "Measuring system", "Fuel dispenser", "Taximeter", "Gas meter". I'll use "Non-automatic weighing instrument".
- type_designations: ["PS60"]
- module_designation: not applicable / null
- description: from characteristics... maybe omit or brief.

Model family: only one type PS60, so don't include model_family? The rule: include ONLY if cert covers >1 model variant. There's just one model. But characteristics table lists "Maximum capacity 60 kg ≤ Max ≤ 150 kg" — that's a range for a single type, not multiple models. So no model_family.

Characteristics type_level:
- accuracy_class: "(III)" → value "III"? The accuracy class is III. Record as accuracy_class: {value: "III"}. Hmm, the recommendation also has accuracy_classes: ["III"].
- maximum_capacity: 60–150 kg → {min: 60, max: 150}, unit "kg"
- verification_scale_interval: e ≥ 20 g → {min: 20, max: null}, unit "g"
- maximum_number_of_scale_intervals: n ≤ 3000 divisions → {min: null, max: 3000}, unit "divisions" (footnote: per partial weighing range — that's part of the cell, maybe a description). Actually "(per partial weighing range)" is a qualifier. Could add footnote-like note. I'll keep unit null and value {min: null, max: 3000}, maybe note in... The schema only allows value/unit/footnote_markers. I could just leave it; or include unit "divisions". Hmm, "divisions" isn't really a unit symbol; keep unit_symbol null. The qualifier "(per partial weighing range)" — I could omit or include as a footnote? Not a real footnote. I'll leave it out or... Better to be faithful: maybe add footnote_markers? No — don't fabricate footnotes. I'll just record max_number_of_scale_intervals with value {min: null, max: 3000}.

Actually maybe record as value: 3000 with max semantics. Keep {min: null, max: 3000}.

- maximum_partial_weighing_ranges: 2 (number of partial weighing ranges). Value 2, unit null.
- temperature_range: -10 °C / +40 °C → {min: -10, max: 40}, unit "°C"
- weighing_ranges: Single interval / Multi-interval → both options. This is a list of configurations. Record as value "Single interval, Multi-interval"? Or config? It says instrument can be single-interval or multi-interval. Record characteristic weighing_range_type with value ["Single interval", "Multi-interval"]? The structured value shape expects value to be number/range/string. I'll use string "Single interval or Multi-interval". Hmm. Alternatively two entries. I'll do value: "Single interval / Multi-interval"? That includes punctuation "/". Fine as string. Maybe better: "single_or_multi_interval": {value: ["Single interval", "Multi-interval"]}. Schema says value: <number | {min,max} | string>. Keep string.

- power_supply_voltage: two rows:
  - 100 V – 240 V AC 50/60 Hz with external adapter → voltage {min:100, max:240} V, type AC, frequency {min:50,max:60} Hz, note "with external adapter".
  - 7,5 V – 15 V DC (supplied by an AC/DC adapter) → voltage {min:7.5, max:15} V, type DC, note "supplied by an AC/DC adapter".

Rule 3 says split into power_supply_voltage, power_supply_frequency, power_supply_type. Here there are two supply options. How to handle? Could use config_level with axis "power_supply_option". Options: "mains via external adapter" and "DC supplied by AC/DC adapter". Let me use config_level:

```
{
  "attribute": "power_supply_voltage",
  "axis": "power_supply_option",
  "values": [
    {"condition": "mains, external adapter", "value": {"min": 100, "max": 240}, "unit_symbol": "V"},
    {"condition": "supplied by AC/DC adapter", "value": {"min": 7.5, "max": 15}, "unit_symbol": "V"}
  ]
},
{
  "attribute": "power_supply_frequency",
  "axis": "power_supply_option",
  "values": [
    {"condition": "mains, external adapter", "value": {"min": 50, "max": 60}, "unit_symbol": "Hz"}
  ]
},
{
  "attribute": "power_supply_type",
  "axis": "power_supply_option",
  "values": [
    {"condition": "mains, external adapter", "value": "AC"},
    {"condition": "supplied by AC/DC adapter", "value": "DC"}
  ]
}
```

That's reasonable. Alternatively type_level simple ones. The config_level approach captures it well.

- application: "Intended to be used for direct sales to the public" → application: {value: "Intended to be used for direct sales to the public"}
- software_identification: version 2.29 → software_version: {value: 2.29}? Version numbers might be "2.29" as string to avoid being treated as number 2.29. Hmm, 2.29 is a version; numeric 2.29 is fine but a version is arguably a string. Rule says numbers not strings. I'll keep 2.29 as number... Actually version identifiers should be strings to preserve trailing zeros etc. But rule 2 says numbers not strings. For version, I'd use string "2.29" since it's an identifier, not a quantity. Hmm. Risky either way. I'll use value: "2.29" as it's a software identifier. Actually, let me reconsider: the rule's intent is about numeric quantities. Version numbers are identifiers. I'll use string.

Recommendation:
- id: R76 (canonical, e.g. "R60" not "OIML R 60")
- edition: 2006
- amendment: null (omit)
- scheme: A|B — R76 certificates under scheme A or B. The certificate number R76/2006-NL1-13.15 — scheme not explicitly mentioned. The certificate text says "This Certificate attests the conformity... with the requirements of the following Recommendation". Not stated whether scheme A or B. Hmm. R76/2006 certs — scheme A vs B is about whether the cert includes type evaluation by the issuing authority or relies on other party's tests. Given it references test reports from NMi (R76/1992-NL-96.20 etc.), likely scheme A? Not certain. Don't fabricate — omit scheme or set null. I'll omit.

Actually wait, "scheme (A|B)" in certificate-level. The cert number format "R76/2006-NL1-13.15" doesn't include scheme letter. Many NMi certs state "under scheme A" or the certificate relates to R76 scheme. Not present → omit.

- accuracy_classes: ["III"]

test_reports[]:
- R76/1992-NL-96.20, 54 pages, role? These are referenced test report numbers — likely type evaluation reports / test reports. Role options: type_evaluation_report | test_report | documentation_file | evaluation_report. These are associated OIML Test Reports. I'll use "test_report" for the older ones (R76/1992 series) and the NMi-13200104-01 dated 3 December 2013 is likely the current test report/evaluation report. Actually all are "OIML Test Report(s)". Use role "test_report" for all. Hmm, but NMi-13200104-01 is the project's test report. I'll mark all as test_report.
